questions.solution:
Let eq. of ellipse be $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $\mathrm{S}$ is $(-\mathrm{ae}, 0), \mathrm{T}$ is $(\mathrm{ae}, 0)$ and $\mathrm{B}$ is $(0, \mathrm{~b})$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{SB}=\sqrt{(0+\mathrm{ae})^{2}+\mathrmb^{2}}$
Also $\mathrm{SB}^{2}=\mathrm{ST}^{2} \Rightarrow 4 \mathrma^{2} \mathrme^{2}=\mathrma^{2} \mathrme^{2}+\mathrmb^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 3 a^{2} e^{2}=a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right)=a^{2}-a^{2} e^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 4 a^{2} e^{2}=a^{2} \Rightarrow e^{2}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.solution: Let equation of ellipse be $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ Since it passes through the points $(-3,1)$ and $(2-2)\begin{aligned}$&\therefore \quad $\frac{(-3)^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{(1)^{2}}{b^{2}}=$1 $\text { and } \frac{(2)^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{(-2)^{2}}{b^{2}}=$1 \\ &\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{9}{a^{2}}+\frac{1}{b^{2}}=$1 \quad $\text{...(i)}$\\ &\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{4}{a^{2}}+\frac{4}{b^{2}}=$1 \quad $\text{...(ii)} \end{aligned}$Multiply by 4 in Eq. (i) and subtracting Eq. (i) from Eq. (ii), 3 a^{2}=32 \Rightarrow a^{2}=$\frac{32}{3}$Substituting in Eq. (i), gives $\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{9 \times 3}{32}+\frac{1}{b^{2}}=$1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & $\frac{1}{b^{2}}=$1-$\frac{27}{32}=\frac{5}{32} \Rightarrow$b^{2}=$\frac{32}{5} \end{aligned}\therefore$ Required equation is $\frac{3 x^{2}}{32}+\frac{5 y^{2}}{32}=$1 $\text { or }$3 x^{2}+5 y^{2}=32

questions.q: If the length of the major axis of the ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$ is three times the length of minor axis, its eccentricity is
questions.solution:
We have

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$

Given,

$\text{Length of the major axis} = 3 \left(\text{Length of the minor axis}\right)$

$⇒ \left(2a\right) = 3 \left($2b\right)$

$⇒ a = 3b$

Now,

$e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{9b^{2}}}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{9}} = \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$

Let the required equation be $\frac{x^2}{b^2}+\frac{y^2}{a^2}=1$ Where $a^2>b^2$ Foci are $(0, \pm c)=(0, \pm 1) \Rightarrow c=1a=$ length of the semi-major axis $=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{5}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\therefore \quad a^2=\frac{5}{4}$ Now, $\quad c^2=a^2-b^2 \Rightarrow 1=\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)^2-b^2\Rightarrow \quad b^2=\frac{5}{4}-1=\frac{1}{4}\therefore$ The required equation is $\frac{x^2}{1 / 4}+\frac{y^2}{5 / 4}=1 \Rightarrow 4 x^2+\frac{4 y^2}{5}=1\Rightarrow \quad 20 x^2+4 y^2=5$

questions.q: For some $\theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right),$ if the eccentricity of the hyperbola, $x^{2} - y^{2}\sec^{2}\theta = 10$ is $\sqrt{5}$ times the~eccentricity of the ellipse, $x^{2}\sec^{2}\theta + y^{2} = 5,$ then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse, is
questions.solution:
For hyperbola& $\dfrac{x2}{10} - \dfrac{y2}{10\cos^{2}\theta} = 1$

The eccentricity of the hyperbola~${e}_{H} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{b2}{a2}} = \sqrt{1 + \cos^{2}\theta}$

For ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{5\cos^{2}\theta} + \dfrac{y2}{5} = 1$

The eccentricity of an ellipse~${e}_{E} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}} = \sqrt{1 - \cos^{2}\theta} = sin\theta$

Given,~${e}_{H} = \sqrt{5}{e}_{E}$

$⇒ 1 + \cos^{2}\theta = 5\sin^{2}\theta ⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now,~the length of the latus rectum~of an ellipse~$= \dfrac{2b^{2}}{a} = \dfrac{10\cos^{2}\theta}{5} = \dfrac{20}{3\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{3}$

questions.q: An ellipse has foci \left(4,2\right),  \left(2,2\right)$ and it passes through the point $P  \left(2,4\right)$. The eccentricity of the ellipse is$
questions.solution:
Let, \left(4, 2\right) = {S}_{1}$ and \left(2, 2\right) = {S}_{2}$ and eccentricity of ellipse is $e$
then ${S}_{1}{S}_{2} = 2ae$ and ${PS}_{1} + {PS}_{2} = 2a$
(where $2a$ is length of major axis)
$⇒ e = \dfrac{{S}_{1}{S}_{2}}{P{S}_{1} + P{S}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2} + 2}$
$⇒ e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} + 1} = \sqrt{2} - 1 = tan\dfrac{\pi}{8}$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{\left(x, y\right) \in R^{2}: \dfrac{y2}{1 + r} - \dfrac{x2}{1 - r} = 1\right\},$ where $r \ne \pm 1 .$ Then $S$ represents:
options: An ellipse whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r + 1}},$ when $r > 1 .$
A hyperbola whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{r + 1}},$ when $0 < r < 1 .$
An ellipse whose eccentricity is $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}},$ when $r > 1$
A hyperbola whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1 - r}},$ when $0 < r < 1$
questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{y^{2}}{1 + r} - \dfrac{x^{2}}{1 - r} = 1$

If $r \in \left(0, 1\right)$ then this curve is a hyperbola whose eccentricity is \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1 - r}{1 + r}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}}.

If $r > 1$ , then this curve is an ellipse whose
eccentricity is $\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{r - 1}{r + 1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}}.$

questions.q: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{9} = 1$. For any three distinct points $P, Q$ and ${Q}^{'}$ on $E$, let $M\left(P, Q\right)$ be the mid-point of the line segment joining $P$ and $Q$, and $M\left(P, {Q}^{'}\right)$ be the mid-point of the line segment joining $P$ and ${Q}^{'}$. Then the maximum possible value of the distance between $M\left(P, Q\right)$ and $M\left(P, {Q}^{'}\right)$, as $P, Q$ and ${Q}^{'}$ vary on $E$, is _____.
questions.solution:
.

In a triangle sides joining the mid-points of two sides is half and parallel to third side

${M}_{1}{M}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}Q{Q}^{'}$

Maximum value of $Q{Q}^{'}$ is $A{A}^{'}$

Hence, maximum value of ${M}_{1}{M}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}A{A}^{'} = 4$
